installation.title: Installation & Setup
installation.subtitle: Use the isolated local profile to develop DeepTrans Studio without touching production services.

prerequisites.title: Prerequisites
prerequisites.description: Before starting the isolated local profile, make sure these tools are available:
items: Node.js ≥ 18.18 (recommended: use corepack to manage Yarn 1.22.22)
Yarn or npm for installing dependencies
Docker Desktop for local dependency containers, started only through the guarded local runner

installDeps.title: Install Dependencies
installDeps.description: Use one package manager for installation; the local runner works with either npm or Yarn.

envConfig.title: Create the Isolated Local Profile
envConfig.description: Copy the committed local template. Do not reuse .env or any production configuration.
envConfig.note: The local runner reads only .env.local, accepts only loopback deeptrans_local services, and disables SMTP, COS, and remote AI by default. Translation-memory vectors are fixed at 2048 dimensions. With LOCAL_ALLOW_REMOTE_AI=no, remote-model features such as translation, chat, embeddings, and model-backed retrieval are expected to be unavailable; that is not a local-startup failure.
envConfig.example:
cp .env.local.example .env.local
# Replace AUTH_SECRET with a random local value.
# Keep LOCAL_ALLOW_REMOTE_AI=no for ordinary development.
# Do not add production database, Redis, COS, or SMTP settings.

initDb.title: Initialize the Isolated Local Database
initDb.description: For a first install, use the wrapper so dependencies, migrations, demo data, and the owned storage bucket can only target the local profile; verify only after setup succeeds.

commands.migrate: npm run local:setup   # Start owned dependencies, migrate deeptrans_local, create the demo account and storage bucket
commands.generate: npm run local:check   # Read-only ownership, credential, storage-bucket, and migration check after setup
commands.seed: # local:setup already creates demo data; no separate local seed command is needed.

startDev.title: Start Local Development
startDev.description: The runner validates .env.local and the owned local services before launching the web app or worker.

step1.title: Prepare the Local Profile
step1.description: Create .env.local once and keep production settings out of it:

step2.title: Start and Initialize Local Services
step2.description: For a first install, setup starts the isolated dependencies, migrates only the local database, seeds the demo user, and creates the owned storage bucket; then verify readiness:
step2.command:
npm run local:setup
npm run local:check

step3.title: Run the Web App and Worker
step3.description: Both commands enter through the isolated runner. Translation-memory imports, vector backfills, and other queued workflows require the Worker:
step3.command:
npm run dev
# In another terminal, start the Worker required by memory imports:
npm run worker
step3.note: yarn dev and yarn worker use the same guarded path. Queued work remains durable and resumes when the Worker becomes ready. The raw commands are internal only.

access.title: Access the Local App
access.description: Visit http://localhost:3000 and sign in with email test@example.com plus the fixed verification code 123456 (not a password) after local:setup succeeds. A successful local start is not proof that a particular end-to-end workflow has been verified; test the workflow you need.

dockerCompose.title: Local Isolation Guardrails
dockerCompose.description: Do not run project Compose commands directly for local development; the wrapper owns the local Compose project and rejects remote Docker daemons.

step1.title: Keep Environments Separate
step1.description: Use .env.local only for local development. Do not copy .env, .env.production, cloud storage, SMTP, or remote database settings into it.

step3.title: Verify the Initialized Local Profile
step3.note: Run local:check after local:setup. local:up is only for restarting already-initialized owned dependencies during recovery or diagnosis.
